where:

u = average wind speed from surface to the stable layer. (m/sec)
Inversion break-up occurs when the nocturnal surface (radiation) inversion becomes deep enough to envelope the plume and the inversion breaks from the surface up through the plume. Briefly, solar heating will cause the surface to warm resulting in an unstable layer growing upward within the inversion. As this unstable air reaches the level of the plume which had been traveling downwind as a narrow cohesive plume, the portion of the plume exposed to unstable air is rapidly mixed downward to the ground. Maximum ground level concentrations result when the inversion breaks to the top of the plume and the entire plume is diffused downward to the surface. The following equation (Turner, 1970) approximates the resultant high surface concentrations beyond the downwind distance X = ut_.
